sources.locator: Contents (PDF pp. 5-6); Chapter 2, Section 2.1 `Independence` through Section 2.1.4 `Constructing Independent Random Variables` (printed pp. 43-55; PDF pp. 47-59); and Section 2.3 `Borel-Cantelli Lemmas` through Theorem 2.3.9 and its proof (printed pp. 67-79; PDF pp. 71-83), opened in the web reader on Friday, September 4, 2026. The design's printed pp. 67-75 range stops before Theorem 2.3.9, so I extended the verified read through that theorem.

contents.reason: This subsection is about convolution formulas for the laws of sums. PT-2 needs independence itself, but the law-of-a-sum machinery becomes load-bearing only when characteristic functions and convolution are developed together on PT-8.

contents.name: 2.1.4 Constructing Independent Random Variables
contents.reason: Durrett's construction work belongs to the next probability page, which owns countable products and the canonical independent-coordinate model. PT-2 uses independence only after such sequences already exist.

Theorem 2.3.2, subsequences characterize convergence in probability
contents.reason: This is a convergence-mode theorem rather than an independence theorem. The commissioned track places that subsequence criterion on PT-4, where almost-sure, in-probability, and L^p convergence are organized together.

contents.name: Theorem 2.3.4, continuous mapping and bounded expectation convergence under convergence in probability
contents.reason: This is another convergence-mode result using Borel-Cantelli as a tool. It belongs with the dedicated PT-4 convergence dictionary rather than as a side branch on the independence page.

contents.reason: Durrett uses the second Borel-Cantelli lemma here to prove a strong-law necessity statement. That conclusion belongs with the PT-6 strong-law page rather than on the PT-2 independence scaffold.
